title: Why your basketball film isn't telling you anything
centralQuestion: Why does recorded basketball footage so rarely become useful basketball information?
pointOfView: Film is only valuable when a coach can return to the moments that mattered without rewatching the whole session. Capture quality decides how much of that is possible, and it is decided before any analysis runs.

hooks.chosen: YOUR CAMERA ROLL ISN'T A FILM LAB.

caption.body:
Most basketball film never becomes useful basketball information.

It gets recorded, buried in a camera roll, and forgotten - or somebody has to rewatch the entire session manually.

We're building Trophy Labs around a simpler loop:
record -> add Film -> keep coaching -> return to the moments

The intelligence underneath should find what the evidence supports and hold back when it doesn't know.

Comment FILM and we'll send you our Courtside Film Setup Checklist for capturing footage that's easier to break down.

resource.title: Courtside Film Setup Checklist
resource.subtitle: Capture footage that is easier to break down.
resource.intro: A one-page setup pass before you press record. Nothing here depends on Trophy Labs - it makes any basketball film easier to review.
items: Put the camera behind or diagonally beside the shooter
Keep the player's full body in frame
Use a stable tripod or fixed surface
Avoid shooting directly into bright lights
Prefer a bright indoor court for the current V1
Keep the ball visible at release and during flight
Avoid frequent zooming or camera movement
Record complete reps instead of stopping immediately after release
Upload the original-quality file when practical

claims.claim: Stable, unobstructed film is easier to analyze than shaky or obstructed film
claims.basis: Direct consequence of how the current Axis vision path works: the player box needs a visible, well-lit subject to hold a lock. Stated as a capture principle, not a measured result.

claims.claim: A recorded session has to be rewatched manually before it becomes useful information
claims.basis: True by construction of the status quo the post describes - a raw camera roll file carries no index of its own.
A stated example of a typical gym session length, not a statistic and not a measured Trophy Labs figure.

claims.claim: Trophy Labs holds back when the film cannot support a conclusion
claims.basis: Axis abstention is an active product rule in this repo, not a roadmap promise.

notes: First campaign. Deliberately says nothing about AI, Codex, or the content engine - the customer cares about basketball film.
